label: Bluetooth
pick_label: Bluetooth will not turn on or connect

b_start.text: Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices. Do you see a Bluetooth on/off switch?
b_start.why: If the switch is missing, Windows may not see a Bluetooth adapter at all, which is a different problem from a device that will not connect.

options.label: Yes, there is a Bluetooth switch

b_toggle.title: Turn Bluetooth off and on
b_toggle.do: Turn Bluetooth off, wait 10 seconds and turn it on. Check that Airplane mode is off. Then try connecting your device again.
b_toggle.why: Switching the radio off and on refreshes the Bluetooth connection.
b_toggle.expect: Nearby Bluetooth devices appear in the list within a few seconds.

b_done_toggle.cause: Bluetooth was switched off or needed a refresh.
b_done_toggle.learn: Bluetooth uses a small radio inside the computer. Airplane mode or a setting can switch it off, and toggling it restarts it.

b_device.title: Check the device itself
b_device.do: Charge or replace the batteries in the Bluetooth device. Move it close to the computer (within 1 to 2 metres). Make sure it is not already connected to your phone or another computer, and turn it off and on.
b_device.why: A flat battery, a long distance, or a device that is already connected elsewhere stops it from connecting.
b_device.expect: The device appears in the list or reconnects.

b_done_device.cause: A flat battery, distance, or the device being connected elsewhere.
b_done_device.learn: Most Bluetooth devices connect to one host at a time. If your headphones are still connected to your phone, your computer cannot reach them.

b_forget.title: Remove the device and pair it again
b_forget.do: Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices, select the device and choose 'Remove device'. Put the device in pairing mode (usually by holding its Bluetooth button until a light flashes). Then choose 'Add device' > Bluetooth and select it.
b_forget.why: The saved pairing can become outdated, and pairing from scratch creates a fresh one.
b_forget.expect: The device appears, connects and shows as Connected.

b_done_forget.learn: Pairing saves a shared key between your computer and the device. If one side forgets it, they cannot reconnect until you pair again.

b_restart.title: Restart the computer
b_restart.do: Use Start > Power > Restart. Choose Restart, not Shut down.
b_restart.why: A restart reloads the Bluetooth driver and services.
b_restart.expect: The Bluetooth switch may appear in Settings after the restart.

b_done_restart.cause: A temporary Bluetooth driver or service fault.
b_done_restart.learn: Fast Startup can keep a stuck Bluetooth driver loaded after a shutdown. A real restart clears it.

b_dm.text: Right-click Start and open Device Manager. Is there a section called 'Bluetooth'?
b_dm.why: If Windows lists a Bluetooth adapter, the problem is likely its driver. If there is none, Windows cannot see one.

options.label: Yes, there is a Bluetooth section
No, there is no Bluetooth section

b_driver.caution: Only uninstall the device named in this step and leave 'Delete the driver' unticked. Windows installs it again when you restart.
b_driver.title: Reinstall the Bluetooth driver
b_driver.do: In Device Manager, expand 'Bluetooth', right-click the adapter and choose 'Uninstall device' (leave 'delete the driver' unticked). Restart the computer and let Windows install it again.
b_driver.why: Windows installs a fresh driver on startup, which replaces a damaged one.
b_driver.expect: Bluetooth appears in Settings again after the restart.

b_done_driver.learn: The Bluetooth driver connects Windows to the adapter. If it is damaged, the adapter can seem missing even though it is fine.

b_pro_missing.reason: Windows cannot see a Bluetooth adapter. Many desktop computers have no built-in Bluetooth, and a small USB Bluetooth adapter can add it. If your computer should have Bluetooth, the adapter may be disabled or faulty, and a technician can check.
causes: No built-in Bluetooth adapter (common on desktops)
Bluetooth adapter disabled in the firmware

b_pro_bt.reason: The safe software checks are used up. The computer's Bluetooth adapter or the device itself may be at fault.
